Rules / Modernization

SK1044 Use string.IsNullOrEmpty

A null test on a string followed by an emptiness test on the same string, or the negation of both.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesS3256

Why

The hand-written form states the check twice and gets its order wrong easily — x.Length == 0 || x == null dereferences null before it tests for it. string.IsNullOrEmpty also carries [NotNullWhen(false)], so the compiler's null analysis learns from the call what it cannot learn from the pair.

Example

Instead of:

if (name == null || name.Length == 0) {
    return "anonymous";
}

Write:

if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(name)) {
    return "anonymous";
}

When it does not fire

x.Length == 0 and x == "" are both reported and are the same check: string == is ordinal value equality that compares lengths first. string.Empty counts as the literal. ⚠ The rule this one must not become is IsNullOrWhiteSpace: x == null || x.Trim().Length == 0 is a different predicate — true for a single space, where IsNullOrEmpty is false — and nothing separates the two shapes except what stands between the receiver and .Length. Two guards therefore do two different jobs: the emptiness test must be on the same expression the null test named, which is what excludes Trim(), and that expression must be a chain of plain names, which is what excludes the double evaluation a call or an indexer would suffer. The receiver must also bind to System.String, so an array's Length is never matched, and the null test must come first. A longer || chain is only matched where the pair is a single subexpression, which left-associativity makes true for x == null || x.Length == 0 || y and false for y || x == null || x.Length == 0. Comments and preprocessor directives inside the expression exclude it.
